decisions.thought: Dragon Dance is the strongest opening: Multiscale lets Dragonite safely boost against Samurott-H, while +1 Speed lets it pressure immediately and threaten a KO with Earthquake next turn. Attacking now risks leaving Samurott healthy while gaining no positioning.

Leading with Ceaseless Edge breaks Dragonite's Multiscale and sets up a layer of Spikes on the opponent's side. With Focus Sash intact, Samurott safely guarantees hazard placement regardless of Dragonite's initial move.

Dragonite outspeeds Samurott-H after the boost, and Earthquake is the strongest reliable hit into its low Defense. It should secure the KO from full, while preserving Terastallization and avoiding unnecessary switching into Ceaseless Edge.

Dragonite is at +1 Atk / +1 Spe with Multiscale broken (78% HP). Samurott-Hisui is at full HP with Focus Sash intact, guaranteeing it survives any single attack. Using Knock Off deals heavy damage and removes Dragonite's item (likely Heavy-Duty Boots or Lum Berry), putting it easily in range for Sucker Punch next turn.
Extreme Speed safely finishes Hisuian Samurott before it can move. Terastallizing is unnecessary against its 1% HP and should be preserved for a more important matchup.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is at critical HP and cannot safely remain: Ogerpon-Wellspring survives Extreme Speed and can easily KO back. Gholdengo is the best switch, resisting Ogerpon’s likely Grass STAB while avoiding Spikes thanks to its Air Balloon, and it can threaten back with Shadow Ball.

Gholdengo is slower and too weakened to safely attack; Ogerpon can likely KO or severely damage it before a second turn. Dragapult resists Ivy Cudgel, outspeeds Ogerpon, and threatens it immediately with Specs Shadow Ball while preserving the healthier defensive options.
Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds unboosted Gholdengo and easily survives a hit if it's Scarfed. Ivy Cudgel (Water-type via Wellspring Mask) easily finishes off Gholdengo at 33% HP with 100% accuracy.

Tera Fire Flamethrower is the decisive play: it gains STAB plus super effectiveness against Wellspring Ogerpon, likely securing the KO while turning Ivy Cudgel into a resisted hit. Dragapult otherwise risks being knocked out immediately, and ordinary Flamethrower may leave Ogerpon alive.

Kingambit is the safest switch: it resists Ogerpon-Wellspring’s revealed Grass STAB, avoids a likely knockout unlike Great Tusk or the weakened options, and threatens a super-effective Iron Head immediately.

Ironhead is the decisive play: it is super effective against Ogerpon-Wellspring and comfortably reaches the knockout threshold from 58%, while Kingambit can survive its Grass-type Ivy Cudgel thanks to Steel’s resistance.

Ogerpon-Wellspring outspeeds Kingambit. The opponent has already used their Tera on Dragapult, meaning Kingambit cannot change its defensive typing. Ivy Cudgel (Water-type via Wellspring Mask) deals heavy neutral damage. Ivy Cudgel is the safest and strongest immediate play to heavily weaken or eliminate Kingambit without risking prediction mindgames.

Ogerpon-Wellspring is at only 22% and has low Defense. Kowtow Cleave is a reliable KO with STAB and higher effective power than Iron Head; Sucker Punch is unnecessary risk if it uses a non-attacking move or switches. Kingambit should remove it immediately.

Opponent's Kingambit is at 47% HP and their Tera has already been used. Ogerpon-Wellspring is at 21.6% HP, susceptible to Sucker Punch. Ivy Cudgel (Water) deals ~45-53%, which reliably KOs Kingambit from this range if they use Iron Head or predict a switch. Even if Kingambit secures the KO with Sucker Punch, we maintain huge momentum with a fresh Iron Valiant and Kingambit in the back to easily clean up the rest of their damaged team. We preserve Tera for later.

decisions.thought: Opposing Kingambit is at 11% HP. Iron Valiant 4x resists Sucker Punch, so even with Supreme Overlord boosts, Sucker Punch will do minimal damage to a full-health Iron Valiant. Moonblast is a reliable 100% accurate STAB move that cleanly finishes off Kingambit without triggering contact effects or lowering defenses.

Ironhead is the decisive play: it is super effective against Iron Valiant and should KO from full, while Kowtow Cleave is ineffective and Sucker Punch is too weak. Kingambit may be KOed first, so attack immediately rather than set up or switch.

Great Tusk is the safest switch: it survives Iron Valiant’s Moonblast, takes only manageable Spikes damage, and its Booster Energy Speed lets it threaten the frail Valiant immediately next turn. Gholdengo is too weakened to risk Spikes plus Moonblast, while Ting-Lu and Dragonite are poor into Fairy STAB.

Iron Valiant likely outspeeds Great Tusk and threatens a knockout with Moonblast. Ting-Lu is the safest switch: its massive HP and Vessel of Ruin substantially reduce Moonblast damage, while preserving Great Tusk for later.

Iron Valiant (364 Speed) naturally outspeeds Great Tusk. Great Tusk has low Special Defense (base 53) and is 4x weak to Fairy. The opponent has already Terastallized, so Great Tusk cannot change its typing. Moonblast is a guaranteed OHKO.

Iron Valiant threatens Ting-Lu with super-effective Moonblast, while Great Tusk and Dragonite are also vulnerable. Gholdengo is the clear pivot: it resists Moonblast and threatens an immediate super-effective Make It Rain KO, despite taking Spikes damage.

Ting-Lu is at 55% HP. Iron Valiant's Moonblast hits Ting-Lu's weaker Special Defense side (even with Vessel of Ruin, 95 BP STAB Moonblast from 339 SpA will easily finish off Ting-Lu from 55%). Close Combat is an alternative, but Ting-Lu's Defense is much higher (base 125 vs 80) and CC lowers defenses. Furthermore, if they switch to Gholdengo (33%) or Dragonite (14%), Shadow Ball or Moonblast covers switches nicely, but Moonblast easily KOs Ting-Lu and deals massive damage to anything switching in except Gholdengo, who Gholdengo/Kingambit can clean up later. Moonblast is the safest, most reliable play.

Great Tusk is the safest pivot: Ting-Lu is doubly vulnerable to Moonblast, while Dragonite is too weak to risk the incoming hit. Great Tusk has enough health to absorb Moonblast and threatens Iron Valiant immediately with a super-effective Headlong Rush.

Headlong Rush is the strongest neutral attack and deals substantially more than Close Combat, which Iron Valiant resists. Great Tusk should survive one Moonblast at its current HP, allowing it to heavily damage or finish Valiant on the following turn. Switching risks losing momentum and exposes the already weakened alternatives.
Iron Valiant naturally outspeeds Great Tusk. Opponent has already burned Tera on Dragapult. STAB Moonblast easily OHKOs Great Tusk at 76% HP through its low base Special Defense.

Ting-Lu is the only switch that can survive Iron Valiant’s Moonblast thanks to its massive HP/Special Defense and Vessel of Ruin. Dragonite is already at 13.6% and is cleanly KOed, while Ting-Lu preserves a usable defensive response.

Ruination is the best threshold play: it immediately removes half of Iron Valiant’s full HP regardless of its unknown item or defensive investment. Switching Dragonite only exposes its 13.6% HP to hazards and Moonblast, while Earthquake is less reliable damage into Valiant’s defenses.

Opponent has only Ting-Lu at 43% and a 14% Dragonite remaining with their Tera already spent. Iron Valiant outspeeds and easily secures the KO on Ting-Lu with Moonblast without incurring the defense drops of Close Combat.

Earthquake is the decisive play: Iron Valiant is at 51%, and Ting-Lu’s STAB Earthquake should KO standard offensive variants from this range. Ruination only chips it to roughly 25%, forcing a risky Dragonite revenge attempt through Spikes.
Moonblast easily finishes off Ting-Lu (10% HP) or catches an incoming Dragonite (14% HP). It is 100% accurate and secures the endgame.
Dragonite is the only remaining Pokémon and must switch in. Its low HP makes the entry hazard damaging, but no alternative action is legal.

Extreme Speed is the only viable action: Iron Valiant outspeeds and Moonblast easily KOs Dragonite, while STAB priority gives the best chance to finish it from 51% HP. Dragon Dance or Roost cannot prevent the immediate knockout, and Earthquake is weaker overall and lacks priority.

Dragonite is the opponent's final Pokémon at 14% HP. Its most likely play to avoid fainting is Extreme Speed. Gholdengo is completely immune to Extreme Speed, making a switch to Gholdengo the 100% safe winning play to finish the game with Choice Scarf next turn.

Earthquake is the only attack with meaningful damage: it hits Gholdengo super effectively and can potentially leave it barely alive, while Extreme Speed is weak. Dragon Dance or Roost cannot prevent Gholdengo from threatening a knockout at Dragonite’s low HP.

Dragonite is the opponent's final Pokémon at 14% HP. Gholdengo is Ghost-type (immune to Extreme Speed) and Choice Scarfed. Shadow Ball is 100% accurate and easily finishes Dragonite off to end the game.
